newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka hopes 1997 budget will revive economy.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka hopes 1997 budget will revive economy.

text.p: Sri Lanka's People's Alliance (PA) government presents the national budget on Wednesday, and faces the tough tasks of reviving a slowing economy, reducing a ballooning deficit and generating more jobs.

Deputy Finance Minister Gamini Lakshman Peiris, who has said he will aim to generate jobs and cut unemployment which is officially at 13 percent, begins his speech for the 1997 calender year budget to parliament at 2.45 p.m. (0845 GMT).
He will announce budget proposals to bridge an overall deficit of 98 billion rupees ($1.72 billion) which is expected to be about eight percent of GDP in 1997, at 4.30 p.m. (1030 GMT).

Peiris, outlining the income and expenditure estimates on October 11, put spending at 283.3 billion rupees, up from 278 billion in 1996 while revenue was pegged at 185.7 billion rupees, up 17 billion rupees from 1996.

Defence spending for 1997 is projected at 44 billion rupees, 22 percent of overall spending, down from an estimated 50 billion rupees this year, most of which went to buy weapons to battle Tamil Tiger rebels fighting for a separate homeland in northern and eastern Sri Lanka.
Peiris has said the economy is expected to grow at four percent this year after being hit by severe drought and power cuts, and bounce back in 1997 to at least last year's growth of 5.5 percent.
